question: Which of the following Constitutional Amendment Bills was passed by the 17th Lok Sabha of India on 17 December 2024?
solution:
The correct answer is __**129th Constitutional Amendment Bill**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **129th Constitutional Amendment Bill** was passed by the **17th Lok Sabha** of India on **17 December 2024**. This bill is significant in the constitutional history of India.
 
• This amendment primarily aimed at **strengthening cooperative federalism** by enhancing the powers of states and providing clarity regarding certain matters of jurisdiction.
 
• The bill was introduced to **address socio-political and administrative issues** concerning governance and federal structure in India.
 
• The **17th Lok Sabha**, elected in 2019, has been active in passing various progressive bills, including the **129th Amendment**, which was one of the landmark decisions of this period.
 
• **Constitutional amendments** require a special majority in Parliament, and this bill successfully garnered the required support, showcasing the commitment of lawmakers toward national progress.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Constitutional Amendments in India:**

 
 
• Under **Article 368** of the Indian Constitution, Parliament has the power to amend the Constitution.
 
• Amendments can be classified into three types: **Simple majority amendments**, **Special majority amendments**, and those requiring **ratification by states**.
 
• India has witnessed several landmark amendments, such as the **42nd Amendment (1976)**, which is considered the most comprehensive and controversial amendment.
 
 
 
• **Role of Lok Sabha in Constitutional Amendments:**
 
 
• The Lok Sabha plays a crucial role in passing constitutional amendment bills. A **two-thirds majority** of members present and voting is required for the approval of such bills.
 
• Members of the Lok Sabha debate the provisions of the amendment extensively before casting their votes.
 
• After Lok Sabha approval, the bill is sent to the Rajya Sabha for deliberation and voting.
 
 
 
• **17th Lok Sabha:**
 
 
• The 17th Lok Sabha was constituted following the **2019 General Elections**, with the Bharatiya Janata Party securing a majority.
 
• It has been instrumental in passing several key legislations, including the **Citizenship Amendment Act (2019)** and the **129th Constitutional Amendment Bill**.
 
• The 17th Lok Sabha is noted for its focus on governance reforms and social welfare schemes.
 
 
 
• **Process of Constitutional Amendment:**
 
 
• An amendment can be introduced in either House of Parliament as a bill.
 
• It must be passed by both Houses with a **special majority**.
 
• In cases involving federal issues, amendments also require the **ratification by half of the state legislatures**.
 
• Once all procedures are completed, the amendment is notified by the President of India.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Legal Considerations:**

 
 
• Constitutional amendments cannot alter the **basic structure** of the Constitution, as ruled by the Supreme Court in the **Keshavananda Bharati Case (1973)**.
 
• The **President of India** plays a ceremonial role in signing the amendment bill into law after parliamentary approval.
 
 
 
• **Historical Constitutional Amendments:**
 
 
• **1st Amendment (1951):** Added restrictions to freedom of speech and expression.
 
• **42nd Amendment (1976):** Introduced the term “**Socialist**” and “**Secular**” in the Preamble.
 
• **73rd and 74th Amendments (1992):** Strengthened **local self-governance** through Panchayati Raj Institutions and Urban Local Bodies.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the 129th Amendment:**
 
 
• It reflects the evolving needs of India's governance framework.
 
• Focuses on addressing **administrative concerns** and **state-specific issues**.
 
• Strengthens the federal structure of India by providing clarity in jurisdictional matters.
